audit.whatIsWrong: The early text tells you to play passive 'for eight seconds' after Yasuo uses Wind Wall. Wind Wall's cooldown is 25/23/21/19/17 — 25 s at rank 1 — and the wall itself only lasts 4 s. Eight seconds is neither number, so the reader gives back roughly seventeen seconds of free window every time.
audit.why: This is the single most decision-relevant cooldown in the matchup and the page's own win condition is built on tracking it.
audit.corrected: The wait rewritten to the real 25 s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 is awarded to Swain at 7/10 while its why says neither champion has a clean setup. Levels 3, 4-5 and First item are given to Yasuo though their whys call them your cleanest trade, your fragment-stacking stretch and 'your widest kill window in the lane'. Packet chart: Skill/Skill/Swain/Swain/Swain/Swain/Yasuo.
audit.why: Four rows contradicted their own explanations at a 53.88% win rate over 399 games. The late-game row correctly stays with Yasuo.
audit.corrected: Row 0 to Skill (5/10), rows 2 and 5 to Swain (7/10), row 3 to Swain (6/10); win[] and phases[].side proposed as pairs.

audit.why: Four spikes present: Level 3 pattern, Level 6 Demonic Ascension against Last Breath, first item, and Yasuo's two-crit-item window. Last Breath at 70/50/30 s genuinely does become a repeatable threat late, which the late-game spike reflects.

audit.whatIsWrong: Way of the Wanderer builds a shield whenever Yasuo is moving and it triggers on the first damage he takes. Nothing on the page mentions it, so the reader plans burst maths that the shield eats.
audit.why: Flagged in missingInteractions for this matchup and confirmed by Riot's passive text. It changes when you commit: chip the shield off first, then root.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now names the Flow shield and tells you to strip it before committing.

edits.before: Levels 1 and 2 are a standoff — your Q pokes but he can Q-dash toward minions to close the gap, and his Windwall blocks both your E projectile and your Q bolts if he reads them correctly. Do not throw E speculatively; bank it for when Windwall is visibly on cooldown. At level 2 walk sideways before casting E so the hand launches from an angle that forces him to misplace Windwall or eat the root. If he Windwalls, note the timestamp and play passive for eight seconds — that is your next free window.
edits.after: Levels 1 and 2 are a standoff — your Q pokes but he dashes through minions to close the gap, and Wind Wall blocks both your E projectile and your Q bolts if he reads them correctly. Do not throw E speculatively; bank it for when Wind Wall is visibly on cooldown. At level 2 walk sideways before casting E so the hand launches from an angle that forces him to misplace the wall or eat the root. The wall itself only stands 4 seconds, and it is down 25 seconds at rank 1 — that whole stretch is your free window.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: His Flow shield eats your opening burst — chip it off before you root.

notes: Wind Wall was described as an eight-second wait; it is a 4-second wall on a 25 s rank-1 cooldown. Chart rows 0, 2, 3 and 5 flipped to packet.levelChart as matched win[]/phases[].side pairs with ratings. Whether Vision of Empire (Swain W) is stopped by Wind Wall is not answerable from Riot's text — the page never claims it either way and I left that alone.
